=================== docs/streams.md
# Work streams — who builds what, and where the streams meet

Written Sat 2026-10-10 for the three people on the team and for their coding agents. The streams are named after
their owners: J = Julien, I = Ivan, O = Orhun. The short table is in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), section "Who does what"; this file is the detail. If you are a coding agent, read
"How the agent works today", then the section of your human's stream, then "Where the streams meet".

The work is split by files. Each file has exactly one stream that may edit it. That is what lets three people and
their agents work at the same time without merge conflicts and without undoing each other's decisions.

## How the agent works today

Everything submitted to Atira is the folder `agent/`. One run goes like this:

1. `agent.py` reads the run (`run.py`: the brief with the bid rules, each website's address and login, the answer
   schema, the expiry time) and opens one browser tab per website (`browsers.py`, `browser.py`).
2. A **lead model** (`Orchestrator` in `agent.py`) reads the brief. It cannot browse. It has three tools:
   - `investigate(site, task)` sends a **browsing sub-agent** (`BrowsingAgent` in `browsing.py`) to one website with
     a task in plain language. The sub-agent drives the browser through a text view of the page (`observe.js`,
     `Tab` in `browser.py`), takes notes, and returns one text report. Several sites run in parallel.
   - `calculate(expression)` does exact decimal arithmetic (`calc.py`).
   - `submit_bid(answer, hints)` checks the answer against the schema, then sends a sub-agent to type the bid into
     the tender website's form, fetch the signing code from the mailbox, sign and confirm.
3. The lead model decides what to ask next from the reports, works out the bid, and submits.

The run's time is split in `agent.py`: investigations end at 65 % of the working time, from 70 % the lead must
submit, and the bid must be entered and signed by 95 %. In a scored run the working time is what the platform
gives (20 minutes: 13 / 14 / 19). In a test run or a local run it is 10 minutes (6.5 / 7 / 9.5), so a development
run reports sooner; the agent tells the two apart by how far away the platform's expiry is.

What is weak in this design, and why the streams exist:

- The reports are free text. A value that was read wrongly, or from the wrong record, is not caught anywhere.
- The lead model applies about 28 bid rules by itself, one calculator call at a time. Money is scored to the cent,
  and 75 of 100 points sit in the positions.
- The final run uses different websites. Anything that only works because of how the public websites look fails
  there.

## Stream J — sites and reading (Julien)

**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
agent has never seen.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js`, `agent/browsing.py`,
`agent/browsers.py`, `agent/tests/test_browser*.py`, `docs/log/julien.md`.

**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream O first).**
- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. `pypdf` is a declared
   dependency since Sat 14:30; before that every PDF came back as "could not be read" in the sandbox.
3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
   which one the site marks as current.
5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
   popups and dialogs.
6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
   another tender is recognisable as such.
7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.

**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.

**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
development story belong to Julien, outside the code.

## Stream I — bid engine (Ivan)

**Goal.** One function that turns collected facts into the answer object, correct to the cent, with no model
involved. The same facts always give the same bid.

**Files only this stream edits (all new).** `agent/facts.py`, `agent/engine/`, `agent/tests/test_engine*.py`,
`docs/log/ivan.md`.

**What the other streams rely on.**
- `facts.py`: typed records (dataclasses) for everything the rules need. Every fact carries where it came from:
  website, document or record, date, sender, revision. This file is the contract between the streams; a change is
  announced in the first line of the commit message.
- One entry point, proposed as `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`, returning an object that matches the answer
  schema in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md), section "Answer schema".

**Rules for the code.**
- `Decimal` only, never `float`. Components stay unrounded; round half-up once at the end (rule 27).
- No model calls, no network, no browser imports. The engine must run in a unit test in milliseconds.
- Tests use invented numbers only. Nothing read from the websites goes into code or tests.
- Missing facts must not crash: a position whose facts are incomplete is left out, and an optional breakdown field
  that is unknown is omitted (omitted means "unanswered", `0.00` means "a known zero"; they score differently).
- If any position has no matching material, the decision is `no_bid` with no positions and total 0.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Read the bid rules in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md) and the full text with `atira challenge rfq`.
   Write each rule down as one or more cases with invented numbers; these become the tests.
2. `facts.py`, first version, covering the core rules only.
3. Core engine: final quantity (latest clarification, withdrawn clarifications, set-to-piece conversion); price
   condition valid on the scenario date at the highest quantity scale reached; discount (latest approval for the
   exact reference, conditional on a minimum order value); lead time (stock shared between positions of the same
   material, no partial allocation); total; arithmetic consistency.
4. Authority and time as functions over facts: only the latest record not after the scenario date, for the exact
   tender reference, from an authorised sender.
5. Advanced pricing layers, one at a time, each with its tests: which parts the discount applies to, currency
   conversion, metal-index surcharge with validity windows, packaging by carton, shared setup pool, project bonus
   in bands allocated by largest remainders, stroke derived from usable travel.

This stream needs no website, no browser and no test run, so it can start at once. Tell stream O as soon as
`facts.py` covers the core rules; O can then start filling it from the reports.

**Done when** `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes in `agent/` and every rule has at least one
test.

**Not this stream.** Reading websites, prompts, form filling.

## Stream O — lead, submission, runs (Orhun)

**Goal.** The run as a whole: the lead model asks the right questions, the answers become facts, the engine prices
them, and one signed bid is submitted before the clock ends, every time.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/agent.py`, `agent/llm.py`, `agent/models.py`, `agent/run.py`,
`agent/calc.py`, `agent/agent.json`, `agent/pyproject.toml`, `agent/uv.lock`, `agent/tests/test_kit.py`,
`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` (except the other two push logs).

**Work, in this order.**
1. Baseline: one sandbox test run of the unchanged agent and its score breakdown. It shows where points are lost
   and sets the priorities of streams J and I.
2. Time budget: done Sat 14:30 (see "How the agent works today"). Open: tune the three shares once a run has
   shown how long entering and signing the bid really takes.
3. Deadline guard: the lead is told to submit at 70 % of the time, but if it never calls `submit_bid` the run
   still ends without a bid and scores 0. Make the submission happen without depending on the lead. After the
   bid is accepted the process must exit within 10 seconds.
4. Reports to facts: have the lead model put what the sub-agents report into the records of `facts.py`, and call
   the engine instead of the calculator, as soon as stream I delivers the first version.
5. Submission: the form, the signing code from the mailbox, signature, receipt check; validation against the
   schema read at run time.
6. `llm.py`: when a provider's environment variable is missing it falls back to the provider's public address.
   Model calls must only go through the platform's proxy, so remove these fallbacks.
7. Dependencies requested by the other streams (`pypdf` for stream J is in).
8. `tests/test_kit.py`: three tests still target the starter kit's `solve()` and fail; rewrite them for the
   current `agent.py`.
9. Test runs for all streams, every `atira submit`, Entire and the repository.

**Not this stream.** How a page is read (`browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`) and how a price is calculated
(`engine/`).

## Where the streams meet

```
websites ──J──> report (text) ──O──> facts (facts.py, owned by I) ──I──> answer object ──O──> signed bid
```

- **J to O:** the report string from `BrowsingAgent.run()`.
- **O to I:** the records in `facts.py`. I defines them, O fills them.
- **I to O:** `engine.build_bid(facts)` returns the answer object.
- You need a change in a file of another stream: describe it to your human, who asks the owner. Do not edit it,
  not even for a one-line fix; the owner may be changing the same lines.
- You need a new dependency: ask stream O. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one owner so the lock file never
  conflicts.
- Local runs with the scouting logins (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`, with `atira models proxy` running) are free
  and unlimited for everyone. Sandbox test runs are limited to two at a time for the whole team and go through
  stream O; ask for one when you need a score.
- Everyone works on their own branch (`stream-j`, `stream-i`, `stream-o`); `main` changes only through pull
  requests. The rules are in AGENTS.md, section "Branches".
- Every push adds an entry to your own push log (`docs/log/<name>.md`, format in AGENTS.md). Read the others'
  new entries after every pull.

## Order of the whole thing (proposal)

1. Now: baseline score (O); core rules as tests and `facts.py` first version (I); per-site report checks (J).
2. Next: core engine wired into the run (I and O); documents and paging reliable (J); second test run.
3. Then: advanced pricing layers (I); submission and deadline guard hardened (O); generalisation check (J).
4. Sunday morning: no new features. The Atira final uses our latest submission that passed review, so the last
   submission before the end must be the most stable one, not the newest experiment. EHL submission is Sunday 12:00.

Newest entry on top. Format and rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), section "Push log".

Newest entry on top. Format and rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), section "Push log".
=================== docs/log/orhun.md
# Push log · Orhun · stream O: lead, submission, runs

Newest entry on top. Format and rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), section "Push log".

## 2026-10-10 14:30 · Time schedule, PDF dependency, stream names J / I / O, branches

- Changed: `agent/agent.py` splits the run's time into three parts: investigations end at 65 % of the working
  time, from 70 % the lead is told to submit, and the submission sub-agent stops at 95 % (it used to run until two
  minutes after the end). The working time is the platform's own in a scored run (20 minutes) and 10 minutes in a
  test run or a local run. `agent/pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` now include `pypdf`. In the documents the streams
  are renamed after their owners (A is now J, B is I, C is O; Uzunov is written as Ivan and his push log is
  `docs/log/ivan.md`), and a "Branches" section says that `main` only changes through pull requests.
- Why: the first test run was still going after 30 minutes without a bid, because the agent planned with the
  test run's two-hour expiry. PDFs could not be read in the sandbox. Three people pushing to `main` at once would
  break each other's runs.
- Checked: the schedule was computed for five situations (test run, local run, scored run, late start) and gives
  6.5 / 7 / 9.5 and 13 / 14 / 19 minutes; an investigation asked for after its time is refused; a small PDF with
  invented text is read. Not checked in the sandbox yet: a new test run follows this push. Three unit tests in
  `tests/test_kit.py` fail before and after this change; they still target the starter kit's `solve()`.
- Learned: a test run's expiry is far later than a scored run's, so an agent that plans with the platform's expiry
  behaves differently in the two.
- For the others: create your branch (`stream-j`, `stream-i`) as described in AGENTS.md, section "Branches", and
  stop pushing to `main`. Commit messages now start with `J:`, `I:` or `O:`. J: PDFs are readable in the sandbox
  from this commit on.
- Next: start a new test run and read its score breakdown; then make the submission independent of the lead.

## 2026-10-10 14:10 · Work streams described in detail

- Changed: new `docs/streams.md` with, for each of the three streams, the goal, the files only that stream edits,

# Entire — talk notes and setup state (Sat 2026-10-10)

Source: Orhun's two voice recordings of the talk by Entire's CEO (ex-GitHub CEO), ~47 min in total, machine-transcribed
on-device; the raw text stays on his machine (`docs/entire-talk-transcript-raw.txt`, git-ignored). It is noisy;
points marked **(unclear)** need confirmation on Discord. CLI facts below were checked against `entire` 0.11.4 on
Orhun's machine.

## What Entire is

- A CLI that hooks into git and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). Every time you or the agent commits,
  the agent **session log** (prompts, responses, tool calls) is stored in the same repository as git objects and
  linked to that commit as a **checkpoint**. Checkpoints are pushed with `git push`.
- His framing: code is the most important artifact, the session log is the second. EHL makes Entire mandatory because
  the organizers want to see those session logs.
- Secrets, passwords and tokens are scrubbed from the logs, but his advice is still: never paste API tokens into the
  agent; put them in an environment variable / `.env` and let the agent read it from there.
- The company also runs a distributed git backend (regions in the US, EU/Frankfurt, Australia, India) and a web
  dashboard where sessions can be browsed, filtered to prompts only, and shared by link.

## Setup steps as demonstrated

1. Install the CLI (installer from entire.io). **Done.**
2. `entire enable` in the project folder; it can create the git repo and an initial commit, then asks which agents
   and whether to send anonymous telemetry. **Done** (all eight agents enabled, telemetry on).
3. **Codex: approve the hooks.** Codex has a trust system; on first start in the folder you must trust the folder
   and approve all seven Entire hooks, otherwise Codex sessions are not captured.
   **Not done:** `entire status` currently reports `7 Codex hook(s) need approval · open /hooks`.
4. When a session is captured the agent shows a line like "Entire will link this conversation to your next commit".
5. Create an empty repository on GitHub (he left it public), add it as `origin`, push. **Not done.**
6. Tell the agent once: "commit, and make sure the Entire session is attached". After that it remembers.
   Expected confirmation on push: `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done` (from the Notion page).
7. On entire.io: log in with GitHub, go through onboarding, pick a region (EU), select the repository. This mirrors
   the GitHub repo to Entire and makes the sessions visible in the dashboard. **Not done.** Whether EHL requires this
   step or only steps 1–6 is **(unclear)**; the Notion page lists only install, enable and the push confirmation.
8. `entire login` in the terminal, which lets the agent search past session logs, including teammates' sessions in
   the same account/repo. He called this the last setup step. **Not done.** Related commands: `entire search`,
   `entire recap`, `entire session list`.

## Advice from the talk that matters for us

- **"Spend an hour tomorrow morning to prepare your pitch."** The jury are humans and weigh the pitch more than the
  product.
- Watch the token budget: do not burn more on API credits than the prize is worth.
- His working model: give agents tasks big enough to run unattended for a long time, with a check at the end, instead
  of many tiny supervised steps. Shared session logs are meant to stop agents repeating each other's mistakes.
- General claims (most code now written by agents, review as the new bottleneck) are opinion, not rules.

## Privacy check — before every commit and before the first push

Entire attaches the full log of every agent session registered in this folder to the next commit, and pushes it.
A session that read anything unrelated to the hackathon must not be attached.

1. `entire session list` — every listed session will be attached. Only sessions started in this folder for
   hackathon work may be there.
2. Remove any other session: `entire clean --session <id> --force`. This clears its state but **not** its data:
   also delete the shadow branch (`git branch -D entire/<base>-<hash>`; it is shared by all sessions on the same
   base commit and is rebuilt on the next turn) and the folder `.entire/metadata/<id>/`.
3. Verify what is left: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <shadow branch> | grep metadata` must list only wanted sessions.
4. A cleaned session registers again on its next turn, so close its window.

State 2026-10-10 ~12:50: one unrelated session was removed this way before anything was committed or pushed.

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

# Work streams — who builds what, and where the streams meet

Written Sat 2026-10-10 for the three people on the team and for their coding agents. The streams are named after
their owners: J = Julien, I = Ivan, O = Orhun. The short table is in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), section "Who does what"; this file is the detail. If you are a coding agent, read
"How the agent works today", then the section of your human's stream, then "Where the streams meet".

The work is split by files. Each file has exactly one stream that may edit it. That is what lets three people and
their agents work at the same time without merge conflicts and without undoing each other's decisions.

## How the agent works today

Everything submitted to Atira is the folder `agent/`. One run goes like this:

1. `agent.py` reads the run (`run.py`: the brief with the bid rules, each website's address and login, the answer
   schema, the expiry time) and opens one browser tab per website (`browsers.py`, `browser.py`).
2. A **lead model** (`Orchestrator` in `agent.py`) reads the brief. It cannot browse. It has three tools:
   - `investigate(site, task)` sends a **browsing sub-agent** (`BrowsingAgent` in `browsing.py`) to one website with
     a task in plain language. The sub-agent drives the browser through a text view of the page (`observe.js`,
     `Tab` in `browser.py`), takes notes, and returns one text report. Several sites run in parallel.
   - `calculate(expression)` does exact decimal arithmetic (`calc.py`).
   - `submit_bid(answer, hints)` checks the answer against the schema, then sends a sub-agent to type the bid into
     the tender website's form, fetch the signing code from the mailbox, sign and confirm.
3. The lead model decides what to ask next from the reports, works out the bid, and submits.

The run's time is split in `agent.py`: investigations end at 65 % of the working time, from 70 % the lead must
submit, and the bid must be entered and signed by 95 %. In a scored run the working time is what the platform
gives (20 minutes: 13 / 14 / 19). In a test run or a local run it is 10 minutes (6.5 / 7 / 9.5), so a development
run reports sooner; the agent tells the two apart by how far away the platform's expiry is.

What is weak in this design, and why the streams exist:

- The reports are free text. A value that was read wrongly, or from the wrong record, is not caught anywhere.
- The lead model applies about 28 bid rules by itself, one calculator call at a time. Money is scored to the cent,
  and 75 of 100 points sit in the positions.
- The final run uses different websites. Anything that only works because of how the public websites look fails
  there.

## Stream J — sites and reading (Julien)

**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
agent has never seen.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js`, `agent/browsing.py`,
`agent/browsers.py`, `agent/tests/test_browser*.py`, `docs/log/julien.md`.

**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream O first).**
- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. `pypdf` is a declared
   dependency since Sat 14:30; before that every PDF came back as "could not be read" in the sandbox.
3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
   which one the site marks as current.
5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
   popups and dialogs.
6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
   another tender is recognisable as such.
7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.

**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.

**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
development story belong to Julien, outside the code.

## Stream I — bid engine (Ivan)

**Goal.** One function that turns collected facts into the answer object, correct to the cent, with no model
involved. The same facts always give the same bid.

**Files only this stream edits (all new).** `agent/facts.py`, `agent/engine/`, `agent/tests/test_engine*.py`,
`docs/log/ivan.md`.

**What the other streams rely on.**
- `facts.py`: typed records (dataclasses) for everything the rules need. Every fact carries where it came from:
  website, document or record, date, sender, revision. This file is the contract between the streams; a change is
  announced in the first line of the commit message.
- One entry point, proposed as `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`, returning an object that matches the answer
  schema in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md), section "Answer schema".

**Rules for the code.**
- `Decimal` only, never `float`. Components stay unrounded; round half-up once at the end (rule 27).
- No model calls, no network, no browser imports. The engine must run in a unit test in milliseconds.
- Tests use invented numbers only. Nothing read from the websites goes into code or tests.
- Missing facts must not crash: a position whose facts are incomplete is left out, and an optional breakdown field
  that is unknown is omitted (omitted means "unanswered", `0.00` means "a known zero"; they score differently).
- If any position has no matching material, the decision is `no_bid` with no positions and total 0.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Read the bid rules in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md) and the full text with `atira challenge rfq`.
   Write each rule down as one or more cases with invented numbers; these become the tests.
2. `facts.py`, first version, covering the core rules only.
3. Core engine: final quantity (latest clarification, withdrawn clarifications, set-to-piece conversion); price
   condition valid on the scenario date at the highest quantity scale reached; discount (latest approval for the
   exact reference, conditional on a minimum order value); lead time (stock shared between positions of the same
   material, no partial allocation); total; arithmetic consistency.
4. Authority and time as functions over facts: only the latest record not after the scenario date, for the exact
   tender reference, from an authorised sender.
5. Advanced pricing layers, one at a time, each with its tests: which parts the discount applies to, currency
   conversion, metal-index surcharge with validity windows, packaging by carton, shared setup pool, project bonus
   in bands allocated by largest remainders, stroke derived from usable travel.

This stream needs no website, no browser and no test run, so it can start at once. Tell stream O as soon as
`facts.py` covers the core rules; O can then start filling it from the reports.

**Done when** `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes in `agent/` and every rule has at least one
test.

**Not this stream.** Reading websites, prompts, form filling.

## Stream O — lead, submission, runs (Orhun)

**Goal.** The run as a whole: the lead model asks the right questions, the answers become facts, the engine prices
them, and one signed bid is submitted before the clock ends, every time.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/agent.py`, `agent/llm.py`, `agent/models.py`, `agent/run.py`,
`agent/calc.py`, `agent/agent.json`, `agent/pyproject.toml`, `agent/uv.lock`, `agent/tests/test_kit.py`,
`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` (except the other two push logs).

**Work, in this order.**
1. Baseline: one sandbox test run of the unchanged agent and its score breakdown. It shows where points are lost
   and sets the priorities of streams J and I.
2. Time budget: done Sat 14:30 (see "How the agent works today"). Open: tune the three shares once a run has
   shown how long entering and signing the bid really takes.
3. Deadline guard: the lead is told to submit at 70 % of the time, but if it never calls `submit_bid` the run
   still ends without a bid and scores 0. Make the submission happen without depending on the lead. After the
   bid is accepted the process must exit within 10 seconds.
4. Reports to facts: have the lead model put what the sub-agents report into the records of `facts.py`, and call
   the engine instead of the calculator, as soon as stream I delivers the first version.
5. Submission: the form, the signing code from the mailbox, signature, receipt check; validation against the
   schema read at run time.
6. `llm.py`: when a provider's environment variable is missing it falls back to the provider's public address.
   Model calls must only go through the platform's proxy, so remove these fallbacks.
7. Dependencies requested by the other streams (`pypdf` for stream J is in).
8. `tests/test_kit.py`: three tests still target the starter kit's `solve()` and fail; rewrite them for the
   current `agent.py`.
9. Test runs for all streams, every `atira submit`, Entire and the repository.

**Not this stream.** How a page is read (`browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`) and how a price is calculated
(`engine/`).

## Where the streams meet

```
websites ──J──> report (text) ──O──> facts (facts.py, owned by I) ──I──> answer object ──O──> signed bid
```

- **J to O:** the report string from `BrowsingAgent.run()`.
- **O to I:** the records in `facts.py`. I defines them, O fills them.
- **I to O:** `engine.build_bid(facts)` returns the answer object.
- You need a change in a file of another stream: describe it to your human, who asks the owner. Do not edit it,
  not even for a one-line fix; the owner may be changing the same lines.
- You need a new dependency: ask stream O. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one owner so the lock file never
  conflicts.
- Local runs with the scouting logins (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`, with `atira models proxy` running) are free
  and unlimited for everyone. Sandbox test runs are limited to two at a time for the whole team and go through
  stream O; ask for one when you need a score.
- Everyone works on their own branch (`stream-j`, `stream-i`, `stream-o`); `main` changes only through pull
  requests. The rules are in AGENTS.md, section "Branches".
- Every push adds an entry to your own push log (`docs/log/<name>.md`, format in AGENTS.md). Read the others'
  new entries after every pull.

## Order of the whole thing (proposal)

1. Now: baseline score (O); core rules as tests and `facts.py` first version (I); per-site report checks (J).
2. Next: core engine wired into the run (I and O); documents and paging reliable (J); second test run.
3. Then: advanced pricing layers (I); submission and deadline guard hardened (O); generalisation check (J).
4. Sunday morning: no new features. The Atira final uses our latest submission that passed review, so the last
   submission before the end must be the most stable one, not the newest experiment. EHL submission is Sunday 12:00.

# Entire — talk notes and setup state (Sat 2026-10-10)

Source: Orhun's two voice recordings of the talk by Entire's CEO (ex-GitHub CEO), ~47 min in total, machine-transcribed
on-device; the raw text stays on his machine (`docs/entire-talk-transcript-raw.txt`, git-ignored). It is noisy;
points marked **(unclear)** need confirmation on Discord. CLI facts below were checked against `entire` 0.11.4 on
Orhun's machine.

## What Entire is

- A CLI that hooks into git and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). Every time you or the agent commits,
  the agent **session log** (prompts, responses, tool calls) is stored in the same repository as git objects and
  linked to that commit as a **checkpoint**. Checkpoints are pushed with `git push`.
- His framing: code is the most important artifact, the session log is the second. EHL makes Entire mandatory because
  the organizers want to see those session logs.
- Secrets, passwords and tokens are scrubbed from the logs, but his advice is still: never paste API tokens into the
  agent; put them in an environment variable / `.env` and let the agent read it from there.
- The company also runs a distributed git backend (regions in the US, EU/Frankfurt, Australia, India) and a web
  dashboard where sessions can be browsed, filtered to prompts only, and shared by link.

## Setup steps as demonstrated

1. Install the CLI (installer from entire.io). **Done.**
2. `entire enable` in the project folder; it can create the git repo and an initial commit, then asks which agents
   and whether to send anonymous telemetry. **Done** (all eight agents enabled, telemetry on).
3. **Codex: approve the hooks.** Codex has a trust system; on first start in the folder you must trust the folder
   and approve all seven Entire hooks, otherwise Codex sessions are not captured.
   **Not done:** `entire status` currently reports `7 Codex hook(s) need approval · open /hooks`.
4. When a session is captured the agent shows a line like "Entire will link this conversation to your next commit".
5. Create an empty repository on GitHub (he left it public), add it as `origin`, push. **Not done.**
6. Tell the agent once: "commit, and make sure the Entire session is attached". After that it remembers.
   Expected confirmation on push: `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done` (from the Notion page).
7. On entire.io: log in with GitHub, go through onboarding, pick a region (EU), select the repository. This mirrors
   the GitHub repo to Entire and makes the sessions visible in the dashboard. **Not done.** Whether EHL requires this
   step or only steps 1–6 is **(unclear)**; the Notion page lists only install, enable and the push confirmation.
8. `entire login` in the terminal, which lets the agent search past session logs, including teammates' sessions in
   the same account/repo. He called this the last setup step. **Not done.** Related commands: `entire search`,
   `entire recap`, `entire session list`.

## Advice from the talk that matters for us

- **"Spend an hour tomorrow morning to prepare your pitch."** The jury are humans and weigh the pitch more than the
  product.
- Watch the token budget: do not burn more on API credits than the prize is worth.
- His working model: give agents tasks big enough to run unattended for a long time, with a check at the end, instead
  of many tiny supervised steps. Shared session logs are meant to stop agents repeating each other's mistakes.
- General claims (most code now written by agents, review as the new bottleneck) are opinion, not rules.

## Privacy check — before every commit and before the first push

Entire attaches the full log of every agent session registered in this folder to the next commit, and pushes it.
A session that read anything unrelated to the hackathon must not be attached.

1. `entire session list` — every listed session will be attached. Only sessions started in this folder for
   hackathon work may be there.
2. Remove any other session: `entire clean --session <id> --force`. This clears its state but **not** its data:
   also delete the shadow branch (`git branch -D entire/<base>-<hash>`; it is shared by all sessions on the same
   base commit and is rebuilt on the next turn) and the folder `.entire/metadata/<id>/`.
3. Verify what is left: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <shadow branch> | grep metadata` must list only wanted sessions.
4. A cleaned session registers again on its next turn, so close its window.

State 2026-10-10 ~12:50: one unrelated session was removed this way before anything was committed or pushed.
=================== agent/README.md
# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"     # the scouting logins, and the model variables pointed at that proxy
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

In PowerShell on Windows, Terminal 2:

```powershell
uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression    # the same exports
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

A Chromium window opens (`HEADLESS=1` hides it). Nothing done with the scouting logins counts, and locally an answer
is printed, never submitted. If `atira` says `Unknown command: models`, run `atira upgrade`.

## Test-run it, then submit it

```sh
atira test-run .   # the sandbox, exactly like a scored run, on the public dataset; opens the run page live
atira submit .     # reviewed, then run once and scored for the leaderboard
```

Both pack this directory without what `.gitignore` excludes.

## Environment

| Variable | Set by | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | runs | the run, at `/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | `atira scout --env` | locally: the brief and the scouting logins |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS` | runs | the sandbox's browsers; locally the kit starts its own Chromium |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env` | the hosted Qwen |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | runs, `atira scout --env`, when Clef is hosted | the hosted Clef |

## Docs

- How a run works: `$API/docs/run-contract.md`
- Building an agent: `$API/docs/building-an-agent.md`
- Fair play, the rules: `$API/docs/fair-play.md`

## Tests

```sh
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

I've read the project docs and looked at the code layout. Here's where things stand for your stream (I, the bid engine).

**The project**
- It's a 24-hour EHL hackathon, Atira track. Our agent turns a German public tender into one signed bid, using four web apps: the tender portal, the supplier portal, an ERP and webmail.
- The repo deadline is Sun 2026-10-11 12:00, with the pitch after that.
- Scoring:
  - **Eligibility:** the right tender reference and a signed bid before the 20-minute clock runs out.
  - **Quality (0–100):** 75 points sit in the positions. Money is compared to the cent.
  - **Cost × time:** used only to break ties.
- The final run uses different software and different data, so nothing may be tuned to the public sites.
- Hard rule: no value from the websites goes into `agent/`. That includes code, tests and comments.

**The code** (`agent/`, about 1,200 lines, Julien's first commit)
- `agent.py` has an `Orchestrator`, the lead model. It has three tools:
  - `investigate(site, task)` sends a browsing sub-agent (`browsing.py`) to one site, and it comes back with a free-text report.
  - `calculate` does decimal arithmetic (`calc.py`, which already has a `round_half_up`).
  - `submit_bid` enters and signs the bid.
- Right now the lead model applies about 28 bid rules itself, one calculator call at a time. That's the weak spot your stream replaces.
- The stack is Python 3.12 and uv, with only three dependencies: openai, playwright and pypdf.

**Your stream I**
- **Files only you edit (all new):** `agent/facts.py`, `agent/engine/`, `agent/tests/test_engine*.py`, `docs/log/ivan.md`.
- **What you deliver:**
  - `facts.py`: typed dataclasses where every fact records where it came from (site, document, date, sender, revision). It's the shared contract; Orhun's stream fills it from the reports.
  - `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`: returns an object matching the answer schema.
- **Rules for the code:**
  - Use `Decimal` only, keep components unrounded, and round half-up once at the end.
  - No model calls, no network, no browser imports.
  - Tests use invented numbers only.
  - A position with incomplete facts is left out rather than crashing the run.
  - An unknown optional field is omitted; `0.00` means a known zero, and the two score differently.
  - If any position has no matching material, the decision is `no_bid`.
- **Order of work:**
  1. Write each rule down as test cases.
  2. First version of `facts.py`, covering the core rules.
  3. Core engine: quantity, price scale, discount, lead time, total.
  4. Authority and time filters.
  5. Advanced pricing layers.
  6. Tell Orhun once `facts.py` covers the core rules.
- **What's still missing:**
  - The repo only has a condensed version of the rules. The full text of rules 01–29 comes from `atira challenge rfq` or the Atira site, and that's the first thing we need.

content.content:
atira.cmd
Atira Challenges CLI

Usage: atira <command> [options]   (or: node atira.mjs <command> [options])

Commands:
  login [--device] [--key <key>]
      Sign in through the browser (--device: with a code instead) and store a personal token, mode 0600; --key stores a team key where there is no GitHub sign-in
  logout
      Revoke the stored token on the server and forget it
  whoami
      Show who you are signed in as, your team and when the token expires
  token
      Print the token in use, for curl: curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" ...
  upgrade
      Download the server's current CLI, check its SHA-256 and replace this file
  challenges
      List the challenges
  challenge <id>
      Print a challenge as Markdown: task, websites, rules, run contract, submitting, answer schema
  scout [--challenge <id>] [--env [--port <port>]]
      Print the published scouting logins for the public websites; --env prints shell exports (CHALLENGE_SCOUTING, CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS, each site's URL, and QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY, CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY pointed at atira models proxy) to run your agent locally against them
  models proxy [--port <port>]
      Run a local proxy on 127.0.0.1 (port 8765) to the free models, QWEN_BASE_URL and CLEF_BASE_URL: it prints the exports
  test-run <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]
      Pack <dir>, run it once in the sandbox on the public data and open its run page; --follow prints its place in the queue, then streams its logs here
  submit <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]
      Pack <dir> and submit it for a ranked run, public and final: review, then one scored run on the public dataset; opens the team page, which follows both; --follow prints the review, each run's place in the queue and its end here
  final [--best-of <1|3>] [--challenge <id>]
      Choose one final attempt or best of three before the final run starts; your own model keys cost up to 3×
  status [<id>] [--challenge <id>]
      Your latest submissions and test runs, or one submission (sub_), test run (reh_) or run (run_)
  logs <run> [--follow]
      Print a test or scored run's logs; --follow polls until the run has ended
  package <id> [--out <dir>]
      Show the package a test run (reh_ or run_), scored run or submission (sub_) of your team used, as uploaded: agent.json and each file's size; --out saves the .tar.gz in <dir>
  cancel <run>
      Cancel a test or scored run that has not finished: its sandbox is removed and the run fails
  leaderboard [--challenge <id>]
      Print the leaderboard
  mcp

content.content:
## The task

One tender, four German websites, one bid.

The agent produces: **One bid**. It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.

## The websites

Each run gets its own logins, in the run's `access`. To look around yourself, use the scouting logins below. Expect what real business software throws at you: popups, session timeouts, outdated documents and look-alike records. Everything your agent needs fits on a 1280×800 screen.

### 1. Tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: The public tender, its bill of quantities, the bidder Q&A that changes quantities, and the bid configurator.
- What makes it hard: Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes and ZIP files, a deadline in another timezone.

### 2. Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: The buyer's technical specification and its revisions.
- What makes it hard: Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables.

### 3. ERP (`erp`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: Your company's materials, stock, lead times and price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales.
- What makes it hard: SAP-style transaction codes, an F4 search popup, status codes, a short session timeout.

### 4. Webmail (Werkpost, `mail`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: Your sales inbox, with the sales director's discount approval and the signing TAN.
- What makes it hard: Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, an archive folder, paging.

### Scout them yourself

Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored.

| Website | URL | Username | Password |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |

## Public and private data

There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.

## Bid rules

The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.

1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.

## Bid rules

The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.

1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%.
